entry.title: Batch extraction with bounded parallel calls and independent recovery
entry.content:
Batch extraction with bounded parallel calls and independent recovery

Allow one exact confirmed batch over prepared source parts, with two concurrent
calls by default and a maximum of four. Reserve the whole batch atomically and
capture/stage each child through the shared extraction lifecycle. Successful
children remain saved when another fails; selected retries bind fresh operation
IDs and exact evidence cleanup, and durable execution receipts resume interrupted
cleanup without repeating an owner decision. Captured replies recover locally.

Expose the same service through Janki Assistant and the CLI, including child
progress, local recovery and retry controls, and a combined real-card HTML
preview. Keep independent staging provenance and disclose duplicate proposals.
Source parts are explicit prepared files; document slicing remains separate.

A prompt cannot enforce dispatch counts, one-use request authority or local file
identity, so the journal and application own those structural checks. No new
Japanese interpretation or content-audit rules are introduced.

Validation: make gates (5248 tests passed, Ruff clean, sample deck built), the
strengthened manifest-binding regression, independent recovery reproductions,
and isolated mutations of dispatch, consent, recovery and Assistant controls.
Independent code reviews covered the journal, application and surfaces.

entry.title: Require complete extraction of every supplied table page
entry.content:
Require complete extraction of every supplied table page

A rich table answer selected only an initial chapter block despite receiving
the complete document. Make whole-document coverage explicit and ask the model
to budget concise, complete cards rather than choose its own sample or promise
a continuation.

Retain printed basic-form columns even when they repeat the headword, and
preserve the source's full semantic header levels so labels keep their long
present/past descriptions. This changes the prompt, not Japanese-inspecting
validation logic.

Validation: make gates (ruff, 5,111 tests, sample deck build).

entry.title: Extract source documents through verified Claude subscriptions
entry.content:
Extract source documents through verified Claude subscriptions

Default extraction to the guarded Claude Pro/Max transport and carry exact
PDF/image inputs through planning, consent, capture, recovery, and staging.
Keep API extraction explicitly configured; a subscription failure never
switches billing providers. Assistant and CLI use the same extraction path.

Preserve source conjugation labels, column order, blank-cell witnesses, and
chapter references. Expand the extraction templates to account for repeated
rows and grouped headers while keeping standalone deck identities separate.

Drain CLI stdout independently of durable frame writes. This prevents the
CLI's bounded shutdown from dropping queued output while each received frame
is still recorded before parsing. Export the full recovery artifact, including
its original manifest, through operations --show-reply.

Make API fixtures explicit and block real Claude subprocesses in tests.
Transport bytes, process cleanup, provenance, and test billing boundaries are
structural contracts that a Japanese-content prompt cannot enforce.

Validation: make gates (ruff, 5,111 tests, sample deck build); real-pipe
truncation regression fails before the fix and with read-ahead removed.

entry.title: Support independent vocabulary decks in Janki Assistant
entry.content:
Support independent vocabulary decks in Janki Assistant

Add explicit standalone vocabulary decks with scoped record identities and
independent Anki progress. Carry the choice through creation, source known-word
filtering, assignment, promotion, previews, and rebuilds. Keep duplicate checks
and JPDB review imports within their appropriate identity scopes.

Allow conversational creation plans to retain previously discussed choices;
the exact confirmation still owns the write. Stack conjugation labels above
their values on mobile while retaining every supplied form in source order.

Scope, identity, and captured-file checks enforce persistent artifact facts.
A card-writing prompt cannot enforce Anki identity or the exact bytes a later
confirmation executes, so these checks belong in repository code.

Validation: make gates; real Anki imports and rebuilds preserve both copies'
review histories; focused mutations verify identity and consent bindings.

entry.title: Offer rendered card previews through Assistant wizard actions
entry.content:
Offer rendered card previews through Assistant wizard actions

Wizard confirmations and proposal reviews now link the actual proposed cards;
preview_cards also renders an existing deck or explicit card selection without
preparing a mutation. Vocabulary, kanji, pattern and conjugation previews use
the real exporters and Anki in a scratch collection. The CLI writes the same
interactive HTML instead of a static vocabulary summary.

Keep proposed bytes, existing media and immutable preview snapshots separate
from confirmation authority. Opening a preview makes no additional provider
call. Source snapshot, scope, media and transport checks bind artifact identity
and exact bytes; these are mechanical contracts a prompt cannot enforce, not
Japanese-content audits.

Validation: make gates (4,967 tests, Ruff, sample build); actual deck and
proposed-service integration; mobile light/dark browser checks, existing audio,
reload stability and no outbound requests; targeted mutations caught.

entry.title: Add dedicated kanji cards and enforce subscription-only development l…
entry.content:
Add dedicated kanji cards and enforce subscription-only development launches

Explicit character targets now produce character notes with stable GUIDs,
KANJIDIC meanings, KanjiVG strokes and source-labelled JPDB reading evidence.
Assistant prepares the exact cards, confirms one apply/build plan, and keeps
progress, recovery and the package download in the conversation. Saved facts
support offline builds; raw JPDB HTML stays outside the repository. Remove
the JMdict word-priority proxy and the superseded acquisition script.

Development and review launches now use a shared subscription-authentication
guard. It removes inherited provider overrides, checks the Pro/Max login in
the dispatch context, and refuses settings or launch-context overrides. Git
review hooks and agent instructions use the tracked launcher, without an API
fallback. Existing explicit paid content providers remain separate.

These structural checks bind authentication, identities, source paths, deck
membership and recovery state. A prompt cannot select its own billing route
before dispatch or prove the bytes used by a later build; no check judges
Japanese content. Regression tests and isolated mutations cover the named
failures. Validation: make gates, actual Anki imports and repeat-import GUID
checks, and mobile/light/dark previews.

entry.title: Prototype on-demand JPDB reading percentages
entry.content:
Prototype on-demand JPDB reading percentages

Capture only requested kanji pages, reuse local cached responses, and refresh
only explicitly. Preserve source reading groups, links, rounded percentages,
bounds and missing values with URL, retrieval time and byte-hash provenance.
Keep full HTML local and record the five-character factual report in Git.

These checks protect HTML structure and cache bytes, not Japanese or model
output; no prompt can supply this artifact-integrity contract. Kanji-card
integration remains a separate design step.

Validation: live five-page acquisition, byte-identical offline and cached-fetch
replays with network disabled, focused tests and mutation checks, and make gates.

entry.title: Prototype Tamaoka reading-frequency acquisition and record source dis…
entry.content:
Prototype Tamaoka reading-frequency acquisition and record source discrepancies

Preserve a seven-character public export and an independent compound-word
lookup for 理, with source requests, hashes, attribution, and a reproducible
standalone diagnostic. Exported reading values do not reconcile with the
compound totals, so the POC leaves usage percentages unverified.

Checks cover CSV structure, exact response bytes, and integer arithmetic;
these are artifact properties, not judgments or inference about Japanese.

Record the owner's requirement for the complete kanji study journey to run
inside Janki Assistant, including review, recovery, and deck delivery.

entry.title: Propose dedicated kanji cards and compare reading-frequency sources
entry.content:
Propose dedicated kanji cards and compare reading-frequency sources

Separate study content types from review directions and propose character
notes with stable identities and contextual vocabulary examples. Record the
owner's agreed meaning-recognition default, distinguishing Show Answer from
the caret for additional readings. Implementation remains a discussion item.

Compare JPDB, Tamaoka, CJKI, Jiten, Ichiran, and NINJAL with primary sources,
distinguishing occurrence counts from dictionary-word prevalence. No reading
provider or existing study content is changed by these documents.

entry.title: Store generated audio in Git LFS
entry.content:
Store generated audio in Git LFS

Convert the current WAVs to LFS pointers without rewriting existing history.
Track recovery audio stages in LFS too, while audition JSON and Markdown
remain ordinary Git files. Compose LFS with the repository review hooks and
hydrate media before bootstrap runs the gates.

Abort a push when its ref capture or LFS upload fails. These checks protect
filesystem and Git transport contracts; a Japanese-writing prompt cannot
ensure that the exact ref bytes reached LFS or that media was uploaded.

Validation: make gates; 31 focused hook/setup tests; 20 named fault mutations;
real local LFS push and fresh-clone download; unchanged hashes for all 1,001
audio-directory files, with 911 WAV pointers and 90 ordinary metadata files.

entry.title: Accept the Assistant agent's progress labels on the action route
entry.content:
Accept the Assistant agent's progress labels on the action route

The three labels recover_agent reports were accepted by the chat
validator and refused by the action validator, so every "Recover
captured result" for an assistant_agent operation failed on its first
progress call, before the journal was read, and the captured answer
could only be discarded with --forget --force. The suite was green
because every recovery test substituted recover_agent.

The labels now belong to both sets. Two tests keep it so: an AST scan
requires every literal the agent reports to be accepted on both routes,
and one recovery drives a real captured turn through
plan_operation_action and execute_operation_action under a validator
that refuses unknown labels.

entry.title: Cut Assistant turn latency and stream the answer as it arrives
entry.content:
Cut Assistant turn latency and stream the answer as it arrives

A message cost about 13 s of local work before the model was contacted,
then about 18 s in a Claude Code call that showed nothing until the
whole result landed.

Local: the repository context was built three times per turn -- the
plan, then two re-plans that guaranteed nothing the request bytes did
not already bind. Staging YAML went through PyYAML's pure-Python loader
and was parsed three times per build, and the source catalog ranked
every source through the completed-card archive to learn only its name.
Now one context build with libyaml, one parse of the review queue shared
by source names, proposal kinds and status, and a names-only catalog:
under a second.

Model: `[assistant] effort` chooses the depth for the one pass that
writes no study content (default medium), bound into argv, environment
and transport so a recovered plan validates from its own bytes. The
Claude Code transport is stream-json with partial messages. Every stdout
line is fsynced to the response spool before it is inspected, the first
text block streams into the thread as a preview, and the validated
structured answer always replaces it. A reply janki cannot read is
captured before it is refused, a failing read kills and reaps the child,
and a PyYAML built without libyaml is refused at import with the fix
named instead of dying on an attribute.

Guardrails rather than conventions: every literal progress label the
adapter emits must be one the validator accepts; a stored Claude Code
command is bound whole, not flag by flag; one broker build parses each
live staging file once; the before-send cancellation lives in one
helper for all four paid paths.

entry.title: Record unanswered Assistant turns instead of wedging the next one
entry.content:
Record unanswered Assistant turns instead of wedging the next one

An ordinary turn whose provider reply carried no answer stayed
result_captured forever. The reply held nothing an owner could act on,
but it still blocked every later question until someone settled it by
hand.

A reply with no answer now decodes to AgentUnansweredError and commits a
durable failed manifest holding its exact provider bytes, so the turn
settles itself and conversation continues. Recovery finishes such a
manifest without another model call.

Only a genuinely unanswered reply may settle itself. Both providers
reach that through an incomplete stop reason or an error envelope, which
decodes to a result with no parsed answer. Every other failure -- an
intent naming an undisclosed resource, structured output that only
failed schema validation, a disk fault -- still holds an answer somebody
could read, so it stays for the owner to decide.

Say what these calls are in owner-facing text. Under a Pro/Max login
there is no per-message charge, so "Paid call needs your decision" read
as if each question were billed; settling one earlier call is now
described as exactly that.

Progress labels are checked against the validator's set rather than kept
in step by hand: _validate_plan refuses an unknown label, so a rename
that misses an emitter fails every use of that action instead of
degrading.
